title: Borrowing
summary: &T lends read access, &mut T lends exclusive write access - ownership stays put.
lecture: A borrow (&value) lets code use a value without taking ownership. The owner keeps the value; the borrower gets a reference that must not outlive it. Any number of shared borrows (&T) may exist at once, OR exactly one mutable borrow (&mut T) - never both simultaneously.

Borrowing is the default answer to 'this function only needs to read my value'. Passing &name instead of name means the caller can keep using name afterwards - the exact fix for most E0382 move errors.
The one-writer-XOR-many-readers rule is what makes Rust memory-safe without a garbage collector: the compiler proves no one can observe a value while someone else mutates it.

example.caption: The caller lends `word` and can still use it after the call.
